name: Fetal Methylmercury Syndrome

criteria.description: Confirmed prenatal exposure to methylmercury through maternal history or biomarker analysis
Presence of global neurodevelopmental delay including cognitive and motor impairment
Sensorineural hearing loss and visual disturbances consistent with methylmercury toxicity
Spasticity and motor dysfunction resembling cerebral palsy
Neuroimaging showing cerebral atrophy or delayed myelination

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Confirmed prenatal methylmercury exposure plus presence of neurodevelopmental delay and at least one additional major criterion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by exposure history and exclusion of other causes

laboratory: Elevated methylmercury levels in maternal or neonatal blood or hair samples
Increased mercury concentration in umbilical cord tissue
imaging: Delayed myelination patterns on brain MRI
genetic: No known genetic mutations; diagnosis based on toxic exposure

distinguishingFeatures: Postnatal methylmercury poisoning rather than prenatal
History of environmental exposure to methylmercury

redFlags: History of maternal fish consumption from contaminated sources during pregnancy
Early onset severe neurodevelopmental delay with sensorineural hearing loss
Neuroimaging showing cerebral atrophy without other known causes
references: Clarkson TW, Magos L. The toxicology of mercury and its chemical compounds. Crit Rev Toxicol. 2006.
Grandjean P, et al. Cognitive deficit in 7-year-old children with prenatal exposure to methylmercury. Neurotoxicol Teratol. 1997.
World Health Organization. Methylmercury. Environmental Health Criteria 101. 1990.
